questions.stem: Arrange the following BATTLES in correct chronological order. 1. First Battle of Panipat. 2. Battle of Khanwa. 3. Battle of Ghaghra. 4. Battle of Chausa.
questions.explanation: Panipat-I = 1526 (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi), Khanwa = 1527 (Babur vs Rana Sanga), Ghaghra = 1529 (Babur vs Afghans + Bengal Sultanate), Chausa = 1539 (Sher Shah Suri vs Humayun). All four touch the early Mughal era. Correct sequence 1526 → 1527 → 1529 → 1539.

questions.stem: Consider the following about AKBAR (1556-1605). 1. He abolished the jizya on non-Muslims in 1564. 2. His 'Din-i-Ilahi' in 1582 was a syncretic spiritual path that did not seek to replace Islam. 3. The Mansabdari system introduced dual ranks: zat (personal rank) and sawar (cavalry rank). 4. The revenue system devised under Raja Todar Mal is known as the 'Zabti' or 'Bandobast' system. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Jizya abolished 1564 (re-imposed by Aurangzeb 1679). Din-i-Ilahi (1582) — a spiritual fraternity, not a state religion, attracted very few followers (Birbal was one). Mansabdari (1571, evolved through Akbar) had zat + sawar. Todar Mal's Zabti (also 'Dahsala') fixed revenue on 10-year averages — the mature stage of the Mughal revenue system.

questions.stem: Match List-I (Mughal emperor) with List-II (architectural masterpiece commissioned during the reign). A. Akbar. B. Jahangir. C. Shah Jahan. D. Aurangzeb. List-II: 1. Bibi Ka Maqbara, Aurangabad. 2. Fatehpur Sikri. 3. Tomb of I'timad-ud-Daulah, Agra. 4. Taj Mahal.
questions.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri — Akbar's new capital c. 1571-85. I'timad-ud-Daulah (tomb of Nur Jahan's father Mirza Ghiyas Beg) — Jahangir's reign, completed 1628 — often called the 'Baby Taj' and the first fully pietra-dura Mughal tomb. Taj Mahal — Shah Jahan, 1632-53. Bibi Ka Maqbara — commissioned by Aurangzeb c. 1660 for his wife Dilras Banu Begum, imitating Taj Mahal but smaller/less opulent.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): Aurangzeb's reign saw a territorial expansion to the south, but the empire entered a long decline soon after his death in 1707. REASON (R): Aurangzeb's lengthy Deccan campaigns drained the treasury and alienated key subjects — Rajputs, Marathas, Sikhs, Jats — leading to fragmentation.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Aurangzeb annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687), extending the empire at its greatest territorial extent in the south. But the 27-year Deccan war (1681-1707), combined with policies that alienated Marathas (Shivaji's rise), Sikhs (execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur 1675), Jats and Rajputs, set the stage for 18th-century Mughal fragmentation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY paired with its author?
questions.explanation: Ain-i-Akbari (a companion volume to the Akbarnama) was also written by ABUL FAZL — not Badauni. Abdul Qadir BADAUNI wrote 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh', a more critical history of Akbar's reign. The other pairs are correct.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the DECLINE of the Mughal empire. 1. The invasion of Nadir Shah (1739) resulted in the sack of Delhi and the carrying off of the Peacock Throne. 2. Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) invaded India multiple times between 1748-1767. 3. The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) decisively weakened Maratha power. 4. The Battle of Buxar (1764) secured Diwani rights for the British East India Company over Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Nadir Shah took the Peacock Throne + the Koh-i-Noor diamond. Abdali invaded 1748, 1749, 1752, 1756-57, 1759-61 (Panipat-III), 1766-67. Panipat-III saw Maratha defeat (Sadashiv Rao Bhau killed) against Abdali-Rohilla-Awadh coalition. Buxar 1764 led to the Treaty of Allahabad 1765 where Shah Alam II granted Diwani (revenue/civil rights) of Bengal, Bihar, Odisha to the EIC.
